parts.prompt: Draw a diagram of the cross-section of the wire as a circle with the current out of the page. On it draw a circular Amperian loop of radius $r<R$ concentric with the wire and an arrow showing the direction of the magnetic field on the loop.
parts.model_answer: A circle concentric with the wire inside its boundary, with the field arrow tangent to the circle and pointing counterclockwise for a current out of the page.

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws a circular loop concentric with the wire and inside its boundary ($r<R$)

common_errors: draws the loop off-center or outside the wire

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws the field arrow tangent to the loop (perpendicular to the radius)
common_errors: draws a radial arrow

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the correct sense, counterclockwise for a current out of the page, by the right-hand rule

common_errors: uses $J\pi r'^2$ without integrating

common_errors: integrates to $r^2$ instead of $r^3$

payload.title: Inserting a dielectric into a charged, isolated capacitor

stimulus.description: An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor has square plates of area $A=200\text{ cm}^{2}$ separated by $d=4\text{ mm}$. It is charged by a $12\text{ V}$ battery and the battery is then disconnected. A dielectric slab of constant $\kappa=4$ that completely fills the gap is then inserted. Use $k=9.0\times10^{9}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^{2}/\text{C}^{2}$ and $\varepsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}\text{ F/m}$.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a diagram of the capacitor in cross-section (two parallel plates, the top plate positive) and draw several electric field lines in the gap before the dielectric is inserted, marking the direction of the field. parts.model_answer: Straight, evenly spaced field lines from the positive plate to the negative plate, perpendicular to the plates and pointing downward; after insertion the field in the gap is weaker (fewer lines per area) because the charge on the plates is unchanged.

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws parallel field lines perpendicular to the plates, evenly spaced
common_errors: draws curved lines in the middle of the gap

rubric_rows.criterion: Marks the direction from the positive plate to the negative plate (downward)
common_errors: draws the arrows toward the positive plate

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the field in the gap becomes weaker (lines less dense) after the dielectric is inserted
common_errors: states that the field becomes stronger

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the capacitance $C$ with the dielectric in place and for the energy $U$ stored in the capacitor after the battery is disconnected and the dielectric inserted, in terms of $\kappa$, $\varepsilon_0$, $A$, $d$ and the initial voltage $V_0$.
parts.model_answer: $C=\kappa\varepsilon_0A/d$; the charge $Q=C_0V_0=\varepsilon_0AV_0/d$ is unchanged, so $U=Q^2/(2C)=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0AV_0^2}{2\kappa d}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes $C=\kappa\varepsilon_0A/d$ with the dielectric
common_errors: divides by $\kappa$

rubric_rows.criterion: Notes that the charge is unchanged, $Q=C_0V_0$ with $C_0=\varepsilon_0A/d$
common_errors: keeps the voltage fixed

rubric_rows.criterion: Obtains $U=Q^2/(2C)=\varepsilon_0AV_0^2/(2\kappa d)$
common_errors: obtains $\kappa\varepsilon_0AV_0^2/(2d)$

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the capacitance with the dielectric in place, in picofarads, and the energy stored after the insertion, in nanojoules.
parts.model_answer: $C=\kappa\varepsilon_0A/d\approx177\text{ pF}$ and $U=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0AV_0^2}{2\kappa d}\approx0.80\text{ nJ}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates $C$ of about 177 with units of picofarads (accept any value within 2 percent)
common_errors: leaves the area in square centimeters

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates $U$ of about 0.80 with units of nanojoules

parts.prompt: A student claims that if the proton's initial speed is doubled, the distance of closest approach to the nucleus is cut in half. Do you agree or disagree with the claim? Justify your answer using conservation of energy.

payload.title: Closest approach of a proton to a nucleus

stimulus.description: A proton moves directly toward the center of a fixed nucleus of charge $+Ze$ with $Z=2$ (treated as a point charge) from a very large distance with speed $v=8\times10^{6}\text{ m/s}$. Use $k=9.0\times10^{9}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^{2}/\text{C}^{2}$, $e=1.60\times10^{-19}\text{ C}$ and $m_p=1.67\times10^{-27}\text{ kg}$.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: A student claims that if the proton's initial speed is doubled, the distance of closest approach to the nucleus is cut in half. Do you agree or disagree with the claim? Justify your answer using conservation of energy.
parts.model_answer: Disagree. At the turning point all of the initial kinetic energy $\tfrac12mv^2$ has become electric potential energy $kq_1q_2/r$, so $r\propto1/v^2$ and doubling the speed cuts the distance to one quarter.

rubric_rows.criterion: Disagrees with the claim
common_errors: agrees that the distance is halved

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies by equating the initial kinetic energy with the electric potential energy at the turning point
required_elements: kinetic energy equals potential energy at the turning point
common_errors: uses the force instead of the energy

rubric_rows.criterion: Shows that the kinetic energy depends on $v^2$ while the potential energy depends on $1/r$, so $r\propto1/v^2$
common_errors: concludes $r\propto1/v$

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the distance of closest approach in terms of $k$, $Z$, $e$, $m_p$ and $v$, and calculate its value in femtometers ($1\text{ fm}=10^{-15}\text{ m}$).
parts.model_answer: $\tfrac12m_pv^2=k(Ze)(e)/r_{min}$ gives $r_{min}=2kZe^2/(m_pv^2)\approx8.6\text{ fm}$ ($1\text{ fm}=10^{-15}\text{ m}$).

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes the energy balance $\tfrac12m_pv^2=k(Ze)e/r_{min}$ (initial potential energy is zero)
required_elements: 1/2 m v^2 = k Z e^2 / r
common_errors: uses $kZe^2/r^2$ for the potential energy

rubric_rows.criterion: Solves for $r_{min}=2kZe^2/(m_pv^2)$
common_errors: omits the factor of 2

rubric_rows.criterion: Obtains about 8.6 with units of femtometers (accept any value within 2 percent)

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: The same proton is shot at a nucleus of charge $+4e$ with the same initial speed. Predict the distance of closest approach compared with the original and justify your prediction.
parts.model_answer: The distance doubles to about $1.72e-14\text{ m}$, because $r_{min}\propto Z$ at fixed speed.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the distance of closest approach doubles
common_errors: states that the distance is halved
states that it is unchanged

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies with $r_{min}=2kZe^2/(m_pv^2)$ (directly proportional to the nuclear charge)
common_errors: argues only that a stronger repulsion keeps the proton farther away
